examples.en: I put the wedding ring on my left ring finger.

examples.ko: 결혼반지는 두 사람의 약속을 보여 주는 상징이에요.
examples.en: A wedding ring is a symbol of the promise between two people.
My wedding ring has gotten too small and is hard to take off.
We chose the same design for our wedding rings.
We decided to go order the wedding rings together too.
We engraved both of our names on the wedding rings.

explain: 반지는 '끼다'라고 하고, 빼는 것은 '빼다'예요. 연인끼리 맞추는 반지는 '커플링'이라고 따로 불러요. 결혼할 때 맞추는 반지라서 '결혼반지를 맞추다'라는 말도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 결혼식 날부터 결혼반지를 계속 끼고 있어요.
phrases.en: I've been wearing my wedding ring ever since the wedding day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반지를 손가락에 넣어 착용한다는 뜻의 가장 자연스러운 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 끼다 is the natural verb for wearing a ring on a finger.

phrases.example: 다음 주에 남편과 결혼반지를 맞추러 가요.
phrases.en: Next week I'm going to order wedding rings with my husband.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 크기를 재고 주문해 만드는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means ordering rings made to fit at a shop.

phrases.en: I took off my wedding ring when I washed my hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끼고 있던 반지를 손에서 벗길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for taking a ring off the finger.

explain_en: For rings, you use '끼다' to wear and '빼다' to take off. A ring a couple orders as a pair is called '커플링', which is a separate word. Since people have them made when they marry, '결혼반지를 맞추다' (to order wedding rings) is also a common phrase.

examples.ko: 고모부가 추석에 맛있는 과일을 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My uncle sent delicious fruit for Chuseok.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 고모부와 낚시를 자주 갔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I often went fishing with my uncle.
My uncle's health has gotten much better lately.
On New Year's Day, I bowed to my uncle.
My uncle runs a small shop in Seoul.

examples.ko: 고모부의 차를 타고 할머니 댁에 갔어요.
examples.en: We went to Grandma's house in my uncle's car.

explain: 아버지 쪽 고모의 남편이에요. 어머니 쪽 이모의 남편은 '이모부'라고 따로 불러요. 높여 말할 때는 '고모부께서는, 고모부께'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: My uncle is in good health these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고모부를 높여서 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific subject form when talking about your uncle.

phrases.en: On New Year's Day I went to my uncle's house to say hello.
phrases.nuance_ko: '집'의 높임말 '댁'을 붙여서 고모부의 집을 공손하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 댁 is the honorific for 'house', used politely for your uncle's home.

phrases.en: My uncle and aunt came to our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부부를 함께 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair used to talk about the couple together.

explain_en: This is the husband of your father's sister. The husband of your mother's sister is called '이모부', a separate word. To show respect, use forms like '고모부께서는' and '고모부께'.

examples.ko: 그 영화에는 백인 배우도 아시아 배우도 나와요.
examples.en: That movie has both white actors and Asian actors.

examples.ko: 이 나라 인구의 절반 정도가 백인이라고 해요.
examples.en: They say about half of this country's population is white.

examples.ko: 설문 조사에는 백인, 아시아인, 히스패닉 같은 항목이 있었어요.
examples.en: The survey had categories like white, Asian, and Hispanic.

examples.ko: 통계에 따르면 이 도시에는 백인과 아시아인이 함께 살아요.
examples.en: According to the statistics, white people and Asians live together in this city.

examples.ko: 미국에는 백인이 많이 사는 지역도 있고 아닌 지역도 있어요.
examples.en: In the US, some areas have many white residents and others do not.

explain: '백인'은 기사나 통계에서 인종을 설명할 때 쓰는 중립적인 말이에요. 한 사람을 소개할 때 피부색부터 말하면 어색하거나 무례하게 들릴 수 있어서, '미국 사람', '프랑스 사람'처럼 나라 이름으로 말하는 편이 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 우리 반에는 백인 학생도 있고 아시아 학생도 있어요.
phrases.en: Our class has both white students and Asian students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인종을 중립적으로 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 꼭 필요한 때만 말하는 것이 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral way to describe race; best used only when necessary.

phrases.en: There are many white people in this city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 지역의 사람들을 통계처럼 설명할 때 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can describe the population of an area in a statistical way.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 백인 인구가 줄고 있어요.
phrases.en: That country's white population is decreasing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기사나 통계에서 자주 보는 말이에요. 일상 대화보다 글에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in articles and statistics; more natural in writing than in casual talk.

explain_en: '백인' is the neutral term used in articles and statistics to describe race. When introducing one person, leading with skin color can sound awkward or rude, so naming the country, as in '미국 사람' (American), sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 손녀딸이 오면 할머니는 항상 용돈을 주세요.
examples.en: Whenever her granddaughter comes, Grandma always gives her pocket money.
Our granddaughter has already become an elementary school student.
Grandfather calls his granddaughter every day.
I took a photo holding my granddaughter at the park.
This outfit is a gift for my granddaughter.

examples.ko: 옆집 할머니는 손녀딸 자랑을 자주 하세요.
examples.en: The grandmother next door often brags about her granddaughter.

explain: '손녀'와 같은 사람을 가리키는데, '딸'이 붙어서 더 다정한 느낌이 나요. 할머니, 할아버지가 말할 때 특히 잘 어울려요. 남자 손주는 '손자'이고, 손자와 손녀를 함께 '손주'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: Grandfather adores his granddaughter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '손녀딸'보다 덜 다정하고 더 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less affectionate and more neutral than 'sonnyeottal'.

phrases.example: 우리 손녀딸이 오늘 학교에서 상을 받았어요.
phrases.en: Our granddaughter got an award at school today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 할머니, 할아버지가 다정하게 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used by grandparents when speaking affectionately.

phrases.en: Grandmother gave allowance to her grandson and granddaughter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남자 손주 '손자'와 함께 묶어 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 'sonja' (grandson) to refer to both grandchildren.

explain_en: It refers to the same person as '손녀', but the added '딸' gives it a warmer, more affectionate feel, especially when grandparents talk. A grandson is '손자', and grandchildren together are called '손주'.

t90.ax: This outfit is a gift for my granddaughter.

examples.en: I was invited to my friend's wedding.
The singer was invited onto the show and sang.
When I'm invited to a housewarming, I prepare a gift.

examples.ko: 초대된 사람들만 이 방에 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only invited people can enter this room.
I wasn't invited to the group chat, so I didn't know the news.

examples.ko: 파티에 초대되고 나니 무슨 옷을 입을지 고민이에요.
examples.en: Now that I'm invited to the party, I'm worried about what to wear.

explain: '초대하다'는 부르는 쪽이고, '초대되다'는 받는 쪽에서 하는 말이에요. 하지만 일상에서는 '초대받다'가 더 자연스러워요. '친구 집에 초대받았어요'처럼요. 행사 공지와 방송에서는 '초대된 손님'이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I was invited to my friend's birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '초대되다'보다 '초대받다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, 초대받다 is more natural than 초대되다.

phrases.en: All the invited guests have arrived.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에서 부른 사람을 말할 때 명사 앞에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun for people called to an event.

phrases.en: I wasn't invited to that gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부르지 않아서 가지 못하는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes not being asked to come.

explain_en: 초대하다 is for the one who invites, and 초대되다 is said from the invited person's side. In daily life, though, 초대받다 is more natural, as in 친구 집에 초대받았어요. In event notices and TV, 초대된 손님 appears often.

examples.en: I buy books online.
I bought a new computer last week.
To buy a ticket, please line up over there.
Where did you buy that bag?

examples.ko: 이 제품은 매장에서만 구입할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy this product only in stores.
The clothes I bought were small, so I went to exchange them.

explain: '사다'와 뜻이 같지만 더 격식 있는 말이라 안내문, 쇼핑몰, 뉴스에서 자주 보여요. 친구와 말할 때는 '샀어요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 짝말은 파는 쪽의 '판매하다'예요.

phrases.en: I buy books at the bookstore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 일상 말로, 친구와 말할 때는 '구입하다'보다 이게 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word with the same meaning, much more natural with friends than 구입하다.

phrases.en: I bought new shoes yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 산 일을 조금 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used to say something was bought in a slightly formal way.

phrases.example: 이 책은 인터넷에서 구입하실 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can purchase this book online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 안내문에서 손님에게 정중하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used politely to customers in shops and notices.

explain_en: It means the same as '사다' but sounds more formal, so you see it in notices, online shops and the news. With friends, '샀어요' is much more natural. Its counterpart on the seller's side is '판매하다'.

dis.h: buy a thing, general and neutral
gh: buy as a customer, often online
buy goods or land for business

p.n: Both are fine; 구매하다 sounds a bit more like online or consumer buying.

examples.en: The delivery food came with wooden chopsticks.
Split the wooden chopsticks in half and use them.
You use wooden chopsticks once and throw them away.
Please give me two more pairs of wooden chopsticks.

explain: 한 번 쓰고 버리는 일회용 젓가락이에요. 보통 붙어 있는 걸 반으로 쪼개서 써요. 세는 말은 '벌'이고, 금속 젓가락은 '쇠젓가락'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Please give me one more pair of wooden chopsticks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젓가락은 한 쌍을 '한 벌'이라고 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair of chopsticks is counted as 한 벌.

phrases.en: At home, I use metal chopsticks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금속으로 만든 젓가락으로, 나무젓가락과 달리 계속 씻어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Metal chopsticks, which are washed and reused unlike wooden ones.

phrases.en: I split the wooden chopsticks and ate the ramen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙어 있는 나무젓가락을 반으로 가를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you split joined wooden chopsticks in two.

explain_en: These are disposable chopsticks, usually joined together so that you split them apart before use. You count them with 벌, and metal chopsticks are called '쇠젓가락'.

examples.ko: 디지털카메라로 찍으면 바로 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you shoot with a digital camera, you can check right away.
Nowadays people take photos with their phones more than with digital cameras.
The digital camera battery has run out.
This digital camera is small and light.
About a thousand photos fit on the digital camera.

explain: 줄여서 '디카'라고 많이 말해요. 필름을 쓰는 '필름 카메라'와 구별할 때 써요. 외래어라서 보통 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: I took a lot of pictures with my digicam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 디지털카메라를 줄인 말로, 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of 디지털카메라, common in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: My digital camera broke, so I took it in for repair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 망가졌을 때 '고장 나다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with 고장 나다 when a machine breaks.

phrases.en: My grandfather still uses a film camera.
phrases.nuance_ko: 디지털카메라와 비교할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing with a digital camera.

explain_en: It is often shortened to '디카'. You use it to distinguish it from a film camera. As a loanword, it is normally written without spaces.

examples.en: The weather warmed up, so I took out my spring clothes.
I needed new spring clothes, so I went shopping.
It's still chilly, so I get cold in just spring clothes.

examples.ko: 겨울옷은 넣고 봄옷은 옷장 앞쪽에 걸었어요.
examples.en: I put away winter clothes and hung spring clothes at the front of the closet.

explain: 계절 이름 뒤에 '옷'을 붙여 여름옷, 가을옷, 겨울옷처럼 말해요. 환절기에는 옷장을 정리하면서 '봄옷을 꺼내다', '겨울옷을 넣다'라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The weather was warm, so I wore spring clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷은 '입다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Clothes go with the verb 입다.

phrases.en: I bought spring clothes at the department store on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이 바뀔 때 쇼핑하며 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said when shopping at a change of season.

phrases.en: When summer comes, I put away my spring clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷장을 정리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when organizing your closet.

explain_en: Adding '옷' after a season name gives words like 여름옷, 가을옷 and 겨울옷. When the seasons change and you tidy the closet, you often say '봄옷을 꺼내다' or '겨울옷을 넣다'.

examples.en: My maternal grandparents' house is a two-story house with a yard.

examples.ko: 언젠가 바다가 보이는 이층집에서 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: Someday I want to live in a two-story house with an ocean view.

examples.ko: 이층집으로 이사한 뒤 계단 오르내리기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Since moving to a two-story house, going up and down the stairs is tiring.

examples.ko: 옆집이 이층집이라 햇빛이 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: The house next door is two stories, so not much sunlight comes in.
Children waved from the balcony of the two-story house.
That two-story house has a red roof.

explain: '이층집'은 건물 전체가 2층인 단독주택을 말해요. 아파트의 2층에 사는 경우에는 그냥 '이층'이라고 해요. 숫자로 '2층집'이라고 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: Our house is a two-story house with a yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자로 쓴 표기로, 글에서 많이 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The numeral spelling, often seen in writing.

phrases.en: I lived in a two-story house when I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사는 집의 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what kind of house you live in.

phrases.en: My father built a two-story house himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 새로 만드는 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about building a house.

explain_en: '이층집' means a detached house that is two stories tall. If you live on the second floor of an apartment building, you just say '이층'. It can also be written with a number, '2층집'.

examples.en: We lit the candles on the cake and sang a song.
The wind came in through the window and the candle went out.
When the power went out, I lit the room with a candle.

examples.ko: 향기 나는 촛불은 방 분위기를 바꿔 줘요.
examples.en: A scented candle changes the mood of a room.

explain: '초'는 물건 자체이고 '촛불'은 타고 있는 불꽃이에요. 생일에는 '초를 꽂다', '촛불을 켜다/끄다'처럼 동사가 달라요. 소리 낼 때는 ㅂ이 세게 나서 [초뿔]처럼 읽어요.

phrases.example: 많은 사람이 광장에 모여 촛불을 들었어요.
phrases.en: to hold a candlelight vigil
phrases.nuance_ko: 촛불을 들고 모여 뜻을 밝히거나 추모하는 집회에 참가한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means taking part in a gathering where people hold candles to voice an opinion or mourn.

explain_en: '초' is the candle itself and '촛불' is the burning flame. On a birthday you 'stick in' a candle ('초를 꽂다') but 'light' or 'blow out' the flame ('촛불을 켜다/끄다'). When said aloud the ㅂ is tensed, so it sounds like [초뿔].

examples.en: I like tomato pasta the most.
I made pasta at home and ate it for lunch.
The pasta is really good at this restaurant.

examples.ko: 파스타 면은 몇 분 동안 삶아요?
examples.en: How many minutes do you boil the pasta noodles?
How about pasta for dinner tonight?
I sprinkled cheese on the warm pasta and ate it.

explain: '스파게티'는 파스타의 한 종류인데, 한국에서는 식당 메뉴에 '파스타'라고 적는 곳이 많아요. 면은 '삶다', 요리는 '만들다'라고 해요. 소스에 따라 '토마토 파스타', '크림 파스타'처럼 이름을 붙여요.

phrases.example: 저는 크림 파스타보다 토마토 파스타가 좋아요.
phrases.en: I like tomato pasta better than cream pasta.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소스 이름을 앞에 붙여 파스타 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the sauce name in front to say which kind of pasta it is.

phrases.example: 먼저 물을 끓여서 파스타 면을 삶아요.
phrases.en: First I boil water and cook the pasta noodles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 면을 물에 익히는 것을 '삶다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Cooking noodles in boiling water is called 삶다.

phrases.en: On the weekend I made and ate pasta with friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 직접 요리해서 먹을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for cooking and eating at home.

explain_en: '스파게티' is one kind of pasta, but many Korean restaurant menus simply list '파스타'. The noodles are '삶다' (boil) and the dish is '만들다' (make). Names follow the sauce, as in '토마토 파스타' and '크림 파스타'.

examples.en: Our team splits the parts and presents.
I took the high part in the choir.
This part is sure to be on the exam.

examples.ko: 파트별로 연습한 뒤에 같이 맞춰 봐요.
examples.en: We practice part by part and then try it together.
The last part of the movie was a little boring.
Many students work part-time at cafes.

explain: 책이나 영상의 한 구간은 '부분'이나 '단원'과 비슷하게 쓰고, 합창·밴드에서 맡은 몫은 '파트'가 거의 정해진 말이에요. 회사에서는 팀 아래 작은 단위를 '파트'라고 부르기도 해요. 시간제 일은 '파트타임'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I sing the low part in the choir.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합창이나 밴드에서 높고 낮은 소리를 나눌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when dividing high and low voices in a choir or band.

phrases.en: We practice by part, then sing together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-별'을 붙여서 파트마다 따로 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-byeol' means doing something separately for each part.

phrases.en: I work part-time at a cafe every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하루 중 일부 시간만 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Work done for only part of the day.

explain_en: For a section of a book or video it overlaps with '부분' or '단원', but for the role you take in a choir or band, '파트' is the set word. Companies sometimes call a small unit under a team a '파트'. A short-hours job is '파트타임'.

t90.ax: I took the high part in the choir.
